items.title: 63519_Wild Bill Davison oral history interview
items.q: we were opposite Fletcher Henderson at that time in the Roseland

ctx.x: Omer -- and, at that time, became the Omer Hicks band. I think that P.T. who later became a big lawyer in New York, is some place, had some money to sort of put into this thing. And, I left the band in Baltimore. I had worked the Roseland Ballroom and all those things and the Bathtub Party and all that stuff and we did a couple of jobs before - after we'd left and I had a chance to go with the, well, I met all those guys like when we were at the Roseland -- I met such guys as Red Nichols and Miff Mole and all of…

and Red told Ross Gorman that maybe he ought to go up and hear me play. And, maybe I could take his place. And, so, Ross Gorman said -- do you think you could handle it - and I said, well, with my reading - if you let me take the parts and take them home -- he said, well, that can be arranged---
